items.title: Stefon Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2020
items.q: I think Bill Watrous did a recording of it and one or two other people are starting to do that too.

ctx.x: Yeah. Speaking of Bobby Hutcherson, I wanted to make sure I thanked you — last night I was checking out some of your recordings and I said, I was sitting in my kitchen and I went, “Oh my God.” And my wife goes, “What’s the matter?” And I said, “Well Stefon did Bobby Hutcherson’s song called ‘Now.’” And I don’t want to spend a lot of time on that but that song used to fascinate me. It was so beautiful. And so thank you for doing a version of it.

Yeah. What a fantastic piece of music, and it functions in the exact way that you hope that any great piece of music will function in that it becomes this phenomenal platform for the expression of a myriad of voices. It’s a so beautiful melody that it’s repeated with an absolutely perfect harmony under it. But it just sort of breathes and it allows you to step into the middle of the song and sing your truth in your own way. It’s a rare thing to come across a composition like that. And unfortunately that’s not a…

Yeah. Going back to the vibes for a minute I have this vision of you as a young man, you know before you could tell the venue what kind of vibes and marimba would be onstage for you, I was picturing yourself like going to a gig with the vibes, and the set-up of that is a bit of a chore, isn’t it?
